anatomy.flutter: registry/foundations/source.json's files array lists ten foundation Dart files (colors.dart, date_format.dart, media.dart, motion.dart, shadows.dart, spacing.dart, surfaces.dart, theme.dart, typography.dart, text_layout.dart, theme_scope.dart) plus two font assets (InterVariable.ttf as 'InterLocal', GeistMono-Variable.ttf as 'GeistMono'), exporting 33 named symbols including ThemeTokens, TextStyles, Shadows, MotionDurations/MotionCurves/MotionTransforms, Radii, Palette, StyledText.
anatomy.web: AGENTS.md states the system is exactly four files — styles/tokens.css, styles/typeset.css, styles/motion.css, styles/utilities.css — plus app/globals.css as the entry that imports them in that order and holds nothing else, mirroring the Dart side's one-file-per-concern split (colors/typography/motion/shadows+spacing) under a single foundation package.

api.flutter: source.json's exports list names ThemeTokens/ResolvedColorMode/ColorMode/Palette for color, TextStyles/TextStyleToken/TextColorRole/Fonts for typography, MotionCurves/MotionDurations/MotionTransforms for motion, Shadows/ShadowStyle/ShadowLayer for elevation, and Radii/BorderWidths/Breakpoints/Containers/LayoutWidths/LayoutHeights/Fluid for spacing/layout — a typed Dart API surface over the same concerns.
api.web: styles/tokens.css defines the CSS custom properties (--color-*, --radius-*, --spacing-*) consumed via Tailwind v4's @theme directive, and lib/utils.ts's cn() (clsx+tailwind-merge) plus components/ui/icon.tsx/icon-swap.tsx are the JS-side API surface referenced by the packet's registryFiles alongside the four styles/*.css files, giving a CSS-variable-plus-utility-function API in place of Dart's typed classes.

states.flutter: source.json is a registry manifest for a Dart package — a files/exports/dependencies list with no runtime widget and therefore no interaction state of its own.
states.web: styles/tokens.css and its sibling files are stylesheets and utility modules, not interactive components; they define tokens consumed by every other component's own state matrix rather than owning states themselves.
states.note: A foundation/token layer has no rest/hover/focus/pressed matrix of its own on either platform — states belong to the components built on top of it.

disabled.flutter: registry/foundations/source.json carries no disabled concept — it is a manifest of files, exports and font/license assets.
disabled.web: The four styles/*.css files and app/globals.css define tokens and utilities, not a disableable control.
disabled.note: Disabled state applies to individual components (buttons, inputs, etc.), which consume this foundation's tokens (e.g. opacity-50, --muted-foreground) rather than the foundation defining disabled behavior itself.

interaction.flutter: source.json declares no widget and therefore no keyboard/pointer/touch/dismissal behavior.
interaction.web: styles/*.css and app/globals.css contain no interactive markup; lib/utils.ts's cn() is a pure string-merging helper and icon.tsx/icon-swap.tsx render presentational SVG wrappers with no interaction handling of their own beyond what a parent component wires.
interaction.note: Interaction is owned by the components that consume these tokens, not by the token/utility layer itself.

semantics.flutter: source.json's fonts array bundles InterVariable.ttf (family 'InterLocal') and GeistMono-Variable.ttf (family 'GeistMono') as first-class package assets with sha256-pinned licenses (Inter-OFL-1.1.txt, Geist-Mono-OFL-1.1.txt) — Flutter has no browser font-loading API, so fonts ship as binary assets registered in the package manifest.
semantics.web: styles/tokens.css and app/globals.css reference font families through CSS custom properties and @font-face-style declarations resolved by the browser's own font loading, with no equivalent sha256-pinned asset manifest — RULES §6 documents which of the four files owns which concern instead.
semantics.note: This is a platform difference rather than a gap: Flutter's package format requires fonts to be declared as versioned, hash-verified assets because there is no browser font-loading mechanism to fall back on, while the web's font strategy is a CSS-level concern resolved by the browser; both achieve the same visual typography (InterLocal/GeistMono) through the mechanism appropriate to their platform, and licensing is tracked in both (OFL files pinned in the Dart manifest; the web's licensing is out of scope for styles/*.css itself).
